tab_overall.caption: Overall average absolute deviation (AAD, \%) from the reference equations of state, pooled over all 37 fluids and 1480 saturation states, with fluid-level bootstrap 95\% confidence intervals in parentheses. tabS_insample_params.caption: Parameters of the in-sample fits: the generalized and the fitted Soave slope parameter $m$, the fitted consistent Twu-91 parameters $(L, M, N)$ and the consistency condition active at the optimum (α‴: third-derivative condition; α″: second-derivative condition; M = 1: bound), for SRK and PR. The Twu-91 parameters are partly interchangeable over the grid (different $(L, M, N)$ give nearly the same $\alpha(T_r)$), so the optimum AAD of {stab:tabS_insample} is better determined than the parameters themselves; the in-sample $\alpha(T_r)$ differs from that of the published parameters [cite:pina2022] by less than 0.8\% anywhere on the grid for every fluid.

tabS_floorloss.caption: The pooled vapor-pressure AAD (\%) of every combination written as the floor of its cubic (the in-sample optimum of the consistent Twu-91 form, Twu-is) plus the parameterization loss of its $\alpha$-function, and the SRK--PR gap (percentage points, SRK minus PR) as the difference of the floors plus the difference of the losses. The floor difference is the contribution of the cubic form at the flexibility of the consistent three-parameter form; the loss difference is what the $\alpha$-function of the row gives up against that form on each cubic. For an $\alpha$-function fitted to the same data by the same procedure on both cubics, the sum of the two is the contribution of the cubic form at that flexibility (fitted Soave form: $0.15 + 0.43 = 0.58$ points); for the published correlations the loss difference also contains their regression histories (Section 3.2.3 of the main text). $^{\dagger}$Component-specific parameters; $^{\ddagger}$in-sample fit.

tabS_pr78.caption: PR76 versus PR78: AAD (\%) of PR with the 1976 correlation for $m(\omega)$ (PR76, used throughout the main text) and with the 1978 modification [cite:robinson1978], $m = 0.379642 + 1.48503\,\omega - 0.164423\,\omega^2 + 0.016666\,\omega^3$ for $\omega > 0.49$ (PR78), for the two fluids of the set above the switch, by reduced-temperature range; the density-anchored translation is re-anchored on the variant. The other 35 fluids, including n-decane ($\omega = 0.488$), are unaffected. At $T_r = 0.50$ the vapor-pressure deviation changes from -26.5\% to -30.1\% for methanol and from -8.3\% to -16.0\% for ethanol.

tabS_srcconst.caption: Model-form error versus input error: pooled AAD (\%) of the fourteen combinations evaluated with the critical constants of the reference equations of state (ref, as in the main text) and with the critical temperatures and pressures listed in the compilation of [cite:pina2022] (src; acentric factors unchanged, same absolute temperatures, same reference values; differences between the two sets of constants up to 0.6\% in $T_c$ and 3.6\% in $p_c$, {stab:tabS_twufit_src}), with the largest per-fluid increase of the vapor-pressure AAD (percentage points, fluid in parentheses) and the number of fluids whose vapor-pressure AAD becomes worse/better. For the fitted reference the compilation constants are those its parameters were regressed with (Section 3.2.4); for the twelve generalized combinations they are an input error on top of the model-form error.

tabS_sens.caption: Input sensitivities of the PR-Soave saturation properties at fixed absolute temperature: logarithmic derivatives with respect to $T_c$, $p_c$ and $\omega$ (central differences, $\pm 0.05\%$ in $T_c$ and $p_c$, $\pm 0.005$ in $\omega$), evaluated for every fluid at the grid point nearest $T_r$ = 0.50, 0.70, 0.90 and 0.985; median over the $n$ fluids present at that $T_r$ with the range over the fluids in parentheses. The SRK-Soave vapor-pressure sensitivities agree within 3\%. At fixed $T$, $T_c$ and $\omega$ every two-parameter cubic gives $p^{sat}$, $\rho'$ and $\rho''$ exactly proportional to $p_c$ and $\Delta h_{vap}$ independent of $p_c$; $\partial \ln p^{sat}/\partial \omega$ is close to $-\ln 10$ at $T_r = 0.70$ because the $m(\omega)$ correlations follow the definition of the acentric factor.

tabS_physics.caption: Physical diagnostics behind the interpretation in Sections 3 and 4 of the main text. Sensitivities are central differences ($\pm 0.01\%$ in $\Omega_a$, which scales $a$ at fixed $T$ and $b$) at $T_r$ = 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9 exactly, for the fluids whose grid includes that temperature (28, 36 and 37 fluids). Effective exponents are least-squares slopes of $\ln(\rho' - \rho'')$ and $\ln \Delta h_{vap}$ against $\ln(1 - T_r)$ over the grid points with $T_r \ge 0.93$; for the cubics the width is normalized by their own critical density, for the reference equations by the reference critical density. The $Z_c$ regression excludes carbon dioxide, which has no grid point below $T_r = 0.70$; the reducing-point $Z_c$ is $p/(\rho R T)$ of the reference equation at its reducing temperature and density, which differs from the critical-point value of Table S2 for methyl chloride (0.269 against 0.294) and n-heptane (0.263 against 0.275), whose reference equations place the critical point 2.3 K and 1.1 K above the reducing temperature. The Clapeyron split writes $\ln(\Delta h_{vap}^{EoS}/\Delta h_{vap}^{ref}) = \ln(\Delta Z_{vap}^{EoS}/\Delta Z_{vap}^{ref}) + \ln(s^{EoS}/s^{ref})$ with $\Delta Z_{vap} = Z'' - Z'$ and $s = d\ln p^{sat}/dT$, each model at its own saturation state; the first term is the volumetric part, the second, the difference of the two rows, follows the $\alpha$-function.
